meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.
Secondary conversational sense ('bigger') (comparative of большой) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Hello! How was it in Hungary?

вовремя.gloss: on time, at the right moment

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'on time'.

examples.text: Ну как же ты не вовремя! Где ты сейчас?
examples.trans: Your timing couldn't be worse! Where are you now?

meanings.note: важный вопрос = an important matter
важный вопрос = an important matter

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'second', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'main' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('the main thing') (neuter главное, used as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: что и требовалось доказать = Q.E.D., which is what needed to be proved

examples.trans: There, which is what needed to be proved!

examples.text: Я обязательно докажу своё кулинарное мастерство.
examples.trans: I will definitely prove my culinary mastery.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'давать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to ask'.

examples.text: Все ваши вопросы задавайте в мэрию!
examples.trans: Address all your questions to the mayor's office!

examples.text: Не задавай глупых вопросов, работай быстрее!
examples.trans: Do not ask stupid questions, work faster!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: mostly in set phrases: иметь совесть, иметь право = to have the right; everyday 'I have' is у меня есть

examples.trans: You have the right to remain silent.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'every', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'culinary' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: I will prove my culinary mastery.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'skill', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: You can't buy skill, got it?

examples.text: Я обязательно докажу своё кулинарное мастерство.
examples.trans: I will definitely prove my culinary mastery.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to begin', forming an aspectual pair with 'начаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Спасибо, теперь для нас начинается новая жизнь.
examples.trans: Thank you, now a new life begins for us.
Our work is only just beginning.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
неделю = for a week; через неделю = in a week

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'some', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: To some, life itself gives a chance.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'shared', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'definitely'.

examples.text: Я тебе оставляю пять миллионов и условный срок.
examples.trans: I'll leave you five million and a suspended sentence.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'boyfriend', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('guy, lad, young man') (informal) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to change one's mind', paired with 'передумывать'.

examples.trans: If you change your mind, come back.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('please') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('you're welcome') (answer to thanks) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Secondary conversational sense ('complete, total, utter') (полный кошмар = a total nightmare) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

поспорить.gloss: to make a bet, argue, wager

meanings.note: perfective verb with с + instrumental

examples.text: Я поспорил, что он сбежит сам.
examples.trans: I bet that he will run away on his own.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'right', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('law') (as a field of study) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('driving licence') (in the plural: права) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: She had a right to the flat.

examples.text: Моя мама имела право на квартиру. Она пенсионерка.
examples.trans: My mother had a right to the flat. She is a pensioner.

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'adventure' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.trans: And the main adventure is only just beginning!

meanings.note: regularly, or as a general invitation: приходи!

examples.trans: If you change your mind, come back. The job is waiting.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'work', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('job') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: сбежать из-под ареста = to escape house arrest

examples.text: Да, он сбежал, чтобы спасти моего ребёнка.
examples.trans: Yes, he escaped custody to save my child.
The prisoner escaped from prison at night.

examples.text: Ты думал, что легко сбежишь отсюда?
examples.trans: Did you think that you would easily escape from here?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.text: Стоять на месте, никто не выходит из кухни без разрешения!
examples.trans: Freeze right there, nobody leaves the kitchen without permission!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'surprise', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
'а то' at the start of a sentence: 'а то мы уже начали беспокоиться' = we were starting to worry

examples.text: А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: We were starting to worry, you see.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (on foot)', paired with 'уходить'.

Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'нижать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to humiliate', forming an aspectual pair with 'унизить'.

examples.text: Она просто унижает меня перед детьми!
examples.trans: She is simply humiliating me in front of the children!

examples.text: Ты зачем так сильно унижал её?
examples.trans: Why did you humiliate her so much?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'morning', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Secondary conversational sense ('people') (plural люди, a different word) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: + accusative: через неделю = in a week
Secondary conversational sense ('through, across') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: From French 'chance' (favorable turn of the dice, from Late Latin 'cadentia').

examples.text: А у меня все шансы есть. Жена, двое детей, не сидел, служил в армии.
examples.trans: And I've got every chance. A wife, two kids, no prison record, I served in the army.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.
